projects.name: AI.SDLC
projects.outcome: Make planning, traceability, evidence, approval, release, and production proof executable and human-readable.
projects.state_reason: v0.2.3 metric-integrity implementation is verified locally; hosted GitHub publication and recorded release proof remain active.

requirements.text: A human project lead can see plans, requirements, work, verification, evidence, blockers, metrics, and releases in one portal.
acceptance: The portal is generated from the same ledger that CI validates.

requirements.text: Required SDLC controls run automatically instead of relying on a person to remember them.
acceptance: Local hooks and hosted CI fail with nonzero exit codes when applicable proof is missing.

requirements.text: A failed task blocks itself without unrelated legacy debt stopping all other work.
acceptance: Task-scoped validation excludes unrelated transition debt while preserving it in the portal.

requirements.text: The system cannot claim a visible or behavioral outcome from packaging, a new URL, or a changed filename alone.
acceptance: Content revisions require artifact identity and passed before/after outcome evidence.

requirements.text: A human project lead sees current LEQ and JouleWork at task, project, and portfolio levels without manually copying scores.
acceptance: Hooks and CI recompute transparent ledger-derived metrics and reject stale generated state.

requirements.text: Invalid work cannot merge or publish through the authorized path, and successful lifecycle events update the ledger without bypassing review.
acceptance: Protected main requires hosted checks; publication depends on a release gate; release and deployment events propose evidence-bound ledger updates through pull requests.

requirements.text: A human project lead can distinguish a priority queue, a named dependency wait, active work, and a genuine actionable blocker.
acceptance: Counts, filters, reasons, clearing actions, and owners represent the declared work state without treating unavailable data as blocked.

requirements.text: Every displayed LEQ, JouleWork, and release field explains whether it is valid, not applicable, awaiting named inputs, stale, or in error.
acceptance: No missing input is rendered as zero, perfect, none, or unexplained unknown; source, scope, freshness, owner, and next action are visible when applicable.

requirements.text: Hosted validation runs on supported application and GitHub Action runtimes without a recurring Node.js 20 deprecation warning.
acceptance: Pinned current actions and the Node.js 22/24 matrix pass on Windows and Linux; historical failed runs remain distinguishable from the current result.

requirements.text: A human project lead can distinguish lifecycle health from traceability coverage and inspect the exact formula, denominator, pending checks, source, and freshness behind every score.
acceptance: Different metric models are labeled and aggregated separately; pending or undeclared checks and old evidence cannot produce a misleading perfect or fresh score.

requirements.text: A public release is called published only after its hosted tag, downloadable asset, digest, and reviewable ledger event exist on GitHub.
acceptance: The protected publication workflow creates one hosted release and one ledger-update pull request; repository publication does not claim a product deployment.

requirements.text: Validate one strict machine-readable portfolio ledger with numbered requirements and linked work, tests, evidence, approvals, artifacts, and releases.
acceptance: Malformed, incomplete, contradictory, or incorrectly linked ledgers fail validation.

requirements.text: Apply stage-specific change, release, post-deploy, and drift gates with selectable project, task, and release scope.
acceptance: Each lifecycle transition asks only for evidence appropriate to that transition.

requirements.text: Generate a responsive human portal from the authoritative ledger.
acceptance: The portal shows progress, verification, evidence, blockers, next actions, metrics, and release state.

requirements.text: Run the gates from repository hooks and GitHub Actions for change, release, post-deploy, and scheduled drift transitions.
acceptance: Actual hosted workflow runs are distinguished from merely committing workflow files.

requirements.text: Bind content-change claims to immutable artifact hashes and passed visual, motion, or behavioral comparison evidence.
acceptance: A delivery-only artifact fails any release that claims changed content.

requirements.text: Compute and publish deterministic traceability-v1 metrics from work, tests, evidence, blockers, and completion state at every ledger level.
acceptance: Task metrics roll up only from applicable valid inputs; missing, stale, and error states invalidate dependent aggregates without inventing scores.

requirements.text: Bind release and deployment automation to real lifecycle events and open reviewable ledger-update pull requests after the relevant gate passes.
acceptance: The authorized publish workflow cannot run before the release gate; production proof is never invented from deployment status alone.

requirements.text: Protect main with pull-request and required hosted-check rules.
acceptance: GitHub API evidence shows direct invalid merges and force/deletion operations are blocked.

requirements.text: Validate and render distinct queued, waiting_dependency, active, blocked, failed, deferred, and unverified work states with actionable blocker ownership.
acceptance: Only blocked and failed count as blockers; waiting dependencies name prerequisites; blocked impediments name a clearing action and owner.

requirements.text: Enforce explicit data-quality contracts and dependent invalidation for LEQ, JouleWork, and release state at schema, lifecycle-gate, sync, and serving time.
acceptance: Positive and negative tests prove explicit states, freshness propagation, named missing inputs, and stage-appropriate failure behavior.

requirements.text: Use supported Node.js 22/24 application tests and current pinned GitHub Action runtimes with automated dependency maintenance.
acceptance: Fresh hosted jobs pass without the deprecated Node.js 20 action-runtime warning and Dependabot covers Actions and npm.

requirements.text: Compute traceability-v2 from explicit verification obligations, keep metric models incomparable, and derive freshness from the oldest contributing evidence.
acceptance: Regression tests cover duplicate pending checks, undeclared required verification, mixed lifecycle/traceability models, and metadata edits that do not renew old evidence.

requirements.text: Publish the registered v0.2.3 artifact through the protected GitHub release path and record the hosted result through review.
acceptance: GitHub hosts tag v0.2.3 and the registered tarball; the downloaded asset digest matches; the release event is merged into the ledger.

evidence.summary: The repository contract, built-in self-test, 24 lifecycle-hook tests, and 14 portfolio/automation tests passed with zero failures, including positive and intentional negative transition cases.
The implemented validator passes complete linked work and rejects malformed, contradictory, stale, unapproved, unproven, or incorrectly packaged states.
The public and private portals rendered at desktop and 390x844 mobile widths with zero browser console errors; private portfolio data remains outside the public repository.
The operator explicitly authorized implementation, verification, and public GitHub promotion of the AI.SDLC upgrade.
The v0.2.0 npm tarball identity was calculated from its actual bytes.
Hosted GitHub Actions passed the executable change gate and the Ubuntu/Windows Node.js 20/24 validation matrix for commit 56831973820d5eb63846a1234b3bd38e4e87dbda.
The repository contract, built-in self-test, 24 lifecycle-hook tests, and 17 portfolio/automation tests passed; protected regression and YAML lint also passed.
The live local portal rendered its task/project/portfolio metrics at desktop and 390x844 mobile widths with zero console errors or warnings.

The live GitHub API confirms protected main requires pull requests, five hosted checks, current-base strictness, conversation resolution, and admin enforcement; force pushes and deletion are disabled.
The v0.2.1 npm tarball identity was calculated from its actual bytes.
Regression cases prove ledger-derived metric rollups, deterministic board sync, lifecycle-event recording, rejection without production proof, and publish-job dependency on the release gate.
The operator required the final completion audit, correction of public release quality, closure of authorized automation gaps, and public promotion only after proof.
GitHub pull request 4 passed the protected change gate and the Ubuntu/Windows Node.js 20/24 validation matrix for commit 3a3714b19c439ad175aebee39acdfa37f9ae5323.
The repository contract, self-test, 24 hook tests, and 21 portfolio/automation tests passed; protected regression passed with explicit positive and negative state/data-quality cases.

The restarted private portal rendered at desktop and 390x844 mobile widths with 9 projects, 0 blocked, 1 queued, 1 dependency wait, explicit metric/release states, and zero console errors or warnings.
Regression cases prove queued work does not inflate blockers, dependency waits name inputs, blockers require clearing ownership, and missing or stale data cannot become invented scores.
The v0.2.2 npm tarball identity was calculated from its actual bytes.
Historical run 35212370450 failed only on Windows because tests/*.test.mjs was not expanded; commit 5683197 replaced it with explicit portable test paths and later Windows runs passed.
Run 35212624876 proved the explicit-path Windows test repair; it supersedes historical run 35212370450 without rewriting that history.
Historical run 35212154194 failed because generated portal timestamps depended on timezone; commit fca1963 made output deterministic and later change gates passed.
Current main runs 35216788410 and 35216788403 passed before the v0.2.2 maintenance branch; historical failures are resolved rather than current blockers.
The operator directed correction of dashboard state semantics, metric/release integrity, and recurring Node.js 20 action-runtime warnings, with verified public promotion.

Pull request 5 passed the protected change gate and Ubuntu/Windows Node.js 22/24 matrix. The hosted logs contain no deprecated Node.js 20 action-runtime warning, and main protection now requires the Node.js 22/24 contexts.

Metric-integrity tests passed for duplicate pending checks, undeclared required verification, model separation, evidence-derived freshness, schema details, deterministic sync, and the complete repository regression suite.
traceability-v2 exposes every verification obligation and keeps lifecycle-v1 scores separate; dashboard regeneration and unrelated metadata no longer refresh contributing evidence time.
The operator authorized correction of misleading LEQ/JouleWork presentation and completion of a real protected GitHub release.

leq.definition: Loop Evidence Quality: requirement linkage, declared and passed verification, evidence linkage, blocker-free execution, and explicit failure penalties.
leq.reason: The synchronized dashboard derives LEQ from registered work items rather than this override.

joulework.definition: JouleWork proxy: evidence-backed useful work credited from linkage, passed verification, evidence, and completed outcomes, minus failure and blocker penalties.
joulework.reason: The synchronized dashboard derives JouleWork from registered work items rather than this override.
